description: What is simply prior to a thing is a cause of its being, as a two-step composition through dependence for being (a middle term distinct from both priority and causation): by the existing OPEN premise, whatever is simply prior to x is something x depends on for its being (only this half of its conjunction is used); by the new OPEN and contested premise, what a thing depends on for its being causes its being. No premise states the conclusion. The grounding-is-not-causation rival falls on the second premise.
